text:
Use retained, completed native work to produce a verified plain-result artifact closure, with separate canonical plan/input/result bindings and parsed-source semantic identity. Canonical digests use the library's portable canonical JSON rendering, not the SHA of printed JSON. Stored entry bytes, library manifest addresses and the Studio archive index retain their own byte hashes. The existing RunRef.archive meaning stays canonical decoded StudyResult digest; Recipe.input stays parsed-source semantic identity.

Scientific completion and storage completion remain distinct. Existing Succeeded/Ready events settle actual science first. Optional native artifact delivery then verifies and stores all accepted artifact content and a future-bound RunStore index before publishing a small exact-job binding fact. An atomic completed-run binding command checks the run/revision/dataset/recipe and enriches only compatible declarations through normal journaling/save. Storage failure leaves truthful Completed/Unbound state and a named artifact refusal; no false stored binding and no automatic Show. Duplicate identical facts are idempotent, conflicting or unrelated facts refuse. Crash leftovers remain immutable orphan/incomplete storage and cannot masquerade as saved bindings.

Canonical input binding is persisted in the typed native facts and library manifest inside the archive; no existing document field is overloaded. This avoids a broad document schema change while preserving the canonical input for verified cold readback. The new binding command receives its own conditional journal version so older readers/writers refuse it without changing old pins.

The initial capability is local to native factories and supplied host sinks, reused by desktop and headless sessions. Payload bytes stay out of progress events, fake/demo backends remain explicitly unbound, and no new backend transport protocol is claimed. Named structural and byte budgets refuse oversized whole-archive materialization; no density/pair/source rows are silently dropped. A stamped execution/result migration is separate work: the current runner produces a plain StudyResult and cannot retroactively attach a forged completion stamp.
